meta.title: IRN Lawbook
meta.scope: Virginia and Maryland laws that protect people from discrimination, police misconduct, wrongful conviction and unfair punishment, plus the federal laws that apply in both states.
meta.notice: Legal information, not legal advice. Summaries are plain-language and leave out exceptions; the official text controls. Laws change every session, so check the official link and the date each section was last checked.

laws.name: Virginia Human Rights Act
laws.enacted: 1987; sexual orientation and gender identity added by the Virginia Values Act, 2020
laws.summary: States Virginia's policy against discrimination in employment, public accommodations, housing and other areas, including because of sexual orientation and gender identity.

laws.name: Human Rights Act definitions
laws.summary: Defines gender identity and sexual orientation for every Virginia anti-discrimination law. Gender identity covers gender-related identity and appearance, with or without regard to sex assigned at birth.

laws.name: Equal access to public places
laws.summary: Bars businesses and other places open to the public, including schools, from refusing service or segregating anyone because of race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and other protected traits.

laws.name: Employment discrimination
laws.summary: Makes it unlawful for employers with five or more employees, or any employer of a domestic worker, to fire, refuse to hire or otherwise discriminate because of race, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and other protected traits.

laws.name: Disability accommodations at work
laws.summary: Requires employers to make reasonable accommodations for known disabilities unless doing so would be an undue hardship.

laws.name: Right to sue for discrimination
laws.summary: Lets a person sue in court for unlawful discrimination after receiving a notice of right to sue, or once 180 days have passed since filing a complaint. The suit must be filed within 90 days of the notice.

laws.name: Ban the box for state jobs
laws.summary: Stops state agencies from asking about arrests, charges or convictions on employment applications, with exceptions for sensitive positions.

laws.name: Local government jobs: orientation and gender identity
laws.summary: Bars counties, cities and towns from employment discrimination because of sexual orientation or gender identity.

laws.name: Virginia Fair Housing Law
laws.summary: Makes it unlawful to refuse to rent or sell, or to set different terms, because of race, sex, source of funds (such as a housing voucher), sexual orientation, gender identity, familial status, military status and other traits.

laws.name: Disability access to public places
laws.summary: Gives people with disabilities the same right as others to use streets, sidewalks, public buildings and other public places, and requires places of public accommodation to remove barriers when that is readily achievable.

laws.name: Disability and housing
laws.summary: Gives people with disabilities the right to equal access to housing accommodations.

laws.name: Disability and the right to vote
laws.summary: Prohibits discrimination against qualified voters with disabilities in voting.

laws.name: Marriage regardless of sex or gender
laws.summary: Declares a marriage between two adults lawful regardless of the sex, gender or race of the parties, and bars clerks from denying a license on that basis. Clergy and religious organizations are not required to perform ceremonies.

laws.name: New birth certificate after change of sex
laws.summary: Lets a person get a new birth certificate showing a change of sex, using a form completed by a health care provider stating they have had clinically appropriate treatment for gender transition. No proof of any medical procedure may be required.
check: clinically appropriate treatment for gender transition
shall not include any requirement for evidence or documentation of any medical procedure

laws.name: Conversion therapy ban
laws.summary: Bars licensed health care providers from practicing conversion therapy on anyone under 18. A violation is unprofessional conduct subject to discipline.

laws.name: Transgender students in public schools
laws.summary: Requires the Department of Education to issue model policies on the treatment of transgender students, covering nondiscrimination and a safe, supportive learning environment, and requires school boards to adopt policies consistent with them.

laws.name: Panic-defense ban: homicide
laws.summary: A victim's actual or perceived sex, gender, gender identity or sexual orientation, or an unwanted advance, is not by itself provocation that excuses or reduces a killing.

laws.name: Panic-defense ban: assault
laws.summary: The same rule for assault and malicious wounding: a victim's sex, gender identity or sexual orientation is not by itself a provocation defense.

laws.name: Bias-motivated assault
laws.summary: Raises the penalty for assault when the victim was chosen because of race, religion, gender, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, color or ethnic or national origin, with a mandatory jail term when there is bodily injury.

laws.name: Hate crime reporting
laws.summary: Requires the State Police to collect and keep data on hate crimes reported in Virginia.

laws.name: HIV and sexually transmitted infection law
laws.summary: Makes it a felony to engage in sexual behavior that poses a substantial risk of transmitting a sexually transmitted infection only when the person intends to transmit it and does transmit it.

laws.name: HIV test results are confidential
laws.summary: Keeps HIV test results confidential, lists the limited exceptions, and lets a person sue for an unauthorized disclosure.

laws.name: Health records privacy
laws.summary: Gives patients a right of privacy in their health records and limits when providers may disclose them.

laws.name: Menstrual data is off limits to warrants
laws.summary: Bars search warrants, subpoenas and court orders that seek menstrual health data stored on apps and electronic devices.

laws.name: No-knock warrant ban
laws.summary: Bans no-knock search warrants. Officers serving a warrant on a home must be in uniform, identifiable and give audible notice before entering.

laws.name: Chokehold and moving-vehicle limits
laws.summary: Bans neck restraints and shooting into moving vehicles unless immediately necessary to protect someone from death or serious bodily injury, and limits kinetic impact munitions such as rubber bullets.

laws.name: Police use of deadly force
laws.summary: Officers may not use deadly force unless they reasonably believe it is immediately necessary to protect someone from serious bodily injury or death, gave a warning if feasible, and had exhausted other options. Courts weigh listed factors, including de-escalation.

laws.name: Duty to intervene
laws.summary: Requires an officer who sees another officer using excessive force to intervene when feasible, give aid to anyone injured and report it.

laws.name: Decertifying officers
laws.summary: Lets the Criminal Justice Services Board decertify law-enforcement and jail officers for listed misconduct, so they cannot simply move to another department.

laws.name: Bias-based profiling ban and stop data
laws.summary: Prohibits bias-based profiling by state police and requires data collection on traffic and investigatory stops.

laws.name: Local police: profiling ban and stop data
laws.summary: The same profiling ban and stop-data rules for local police and sheriffs.

laws.name: Odor of marijuana is not grounds to search
laws.summary: Officers may not stop, search or seize anyone, and no warrant may issue, based only on the odor of marijuana. Evidence found that way is inadmissible, even with consent.

laws.name: Limits on pretext stops: inspection stickers
laws.summary: Officers may not stop a car for an expired inspection sticker until the fourth month after it expires. Evidence from an unlawful stop is inadmissible.
check: No law-enforcement officer shall stop a motor vehicle due to an expired vehicle inspection sticker

laws.name: Body-worn camera policies
laws.summary: Requires a police agency to adopt a written policy on body-worn cameras before buying or deploying them.

laws.name: Deaths in custody report
laws.summary: Requires an annual public report on civilian deaths in the custody of law enforcement and corrections.

laws.name: Virginia Freedom of Information Act
laws.summary: States that government records and meetings are open to the public, and that exemptions are read narrowly.

laws.name: Requesting public records
laws.summary: Gives Virginia citizens the right to inspect and copy public records and sets the response deadline and charges.

laws.name: Police investigative files
laws.summary: Requires release of criminal incident information and lets immediate family members of a deceased person obtain criminal investigative files once a case is no longer ongoing, with limits.

laws.name: Expungement of charges
laws.summary: Lets a person who was charged but not convicted petition to expunge the police and court records, with no filing fee. A person whose name was used by someone else who was arrested can petition too.

laws.name: What sealing means
laws.summary: Defines sealing: a sealed record is hidden from the public and from most background checks, and the person may deny the arrest or conviction in most settings.

laws.name: Automatic sealing of convictions
laws.summary: Automatically seals convictions for a short list of misdemeanors, such as petit larceny, trespass and disorderly conduct, after a waiting period, subject to conditions in the section.

laws.name: Sealing by petition
laws.summary: Lets a person petition, with no filing fee, to seal misdemeanors, Class 5 and 6 felonies and some larceny convictions or deferred-and-dismissed charges, after the waiting period.
check: shall not be required to pay any court fees

laws.name: Sealing old marijuana possession records
laws.summary: Seals former marijuana possession offenses without a court order.

laws.name: Eviction record expungement
laws.summary: Automatically expunges an eviction case that was dismissed (after 30 days) or nonsuited (after six months) when no order of possession was entered. A tenant who won the case can petition for expungement without a hearing.

laws.name: Juvenile court records
laws.summary: Requires juvenile court files to be destroyed once the person turns 19 and five years have passed since their last hearing. Records of offenses that would be felonies for an adult are kept.
check: attained the age of 19 years and five years

laws.name: Actual innocence: biological evidence
laws.summary: Lets a person convicted of a felony, or adjudicated delinquent for a felony-level act, petition the Supreme Court of Virginia for a writ of actual innocence based on biological (DNA) evidence.
check: Supreme Court shall have the authority

laws.name: Actual innocence: other evidence
laws.summary: Lets a person convicted of a felony, or adjudicated delinquent for a felony-level act, petition the Court of Appeals for a writ of actual innocence based on previously unknown or unavailable evidence that is not biological.
check: Court of Appeals shall have the authority

laws.name: Compensation for wrongful incarceration
laws.summary: Compensates a person wrongfully incarcerated for a felony at $55,000 per year, adjusted each year for inflation, plus a $15,000 transition grant and up to $10,000 for career and technical training. Who counts as wrongfully incarcerated is defined in § 8.01-195.10.

laws.name: Preserving DNA evidence
laws.summary: On motion of a person convicted of a felony, the court must order human biological evidence in the case stored and preserved for up to 15 years, so it can be tested later.

laws.name: Pretrial release
laws.summary: Requires release before trial unless there is probable cause to believe the person will not appear or is an unreasonable danger.

laws.name: Judge sentencing by default
laws.summary: The judge sets the sentence unless the defendant asks in writing, at least 30 days before trial, for the jury to do it.
check: requested that the jury ascertain punishment

laws.name: Felony punishments (no death penalty)
laws.summary: Sets the punishment for each class of felony. The most serious, Class 1, now carries life imprisonment.

laws.name: Earned sentence credits
laws.summary: Sets who is eligible for earned sentence credits that shorten time served.

laws.name: Geriatric release
laws.summary: Lets people aged 65 who have served five years, or aged 60 who have served ten, petition the Parole Board for conditional release. Class 1 felonies are excluded.

laws.name: Parole limits and juvenile second looks
laws.summary: Ends parole for felonies committed on or after January 1, 1995, with exceptions. People sentenced for crimes committed as juveniles become eligible for parole after serving 20 years.
check: committed while the person was a juvenile

laws.name: Limits on probation revocation
laws.summary: Caps the jail time a court may impose for technical violations of probation.

laws.name: Deferred disposition for autism and intellectual disability
laws.summary: Lets a court defer and dismiss some charges when the defendant has autism or an intellectual or developmental disability that contributed to the offense.

laws.name: Limits on solitary confinement
laws.summary: Limits restorative housing (solitary confinement) in state prisons, requires medical and mental health evaluations, and requires at least four hours a day out of cell except during a lockdown.

laws.name: Transfer of juveniles to adult court
laws.summary: Sets when a juvenile 14 or older may be tried as an adult, and requires a hearing for 16- and 17-year-olds charged with murder or aggravated malicious wounding.

laws.name: No shackling of children in court
laws.summary: Bars physical restraints on juveniles in court, with narrow exceptions.

laws.name: Felony disenfranchisement
laws.summary: Under the Constitution as it stands, a person convicted of a felony cannot vote until the Governor or other authority restores their civil rights. An amendment to restore voting rights on release is on the November 3, 2026 ballot.

laws.name: Voting rights on release (pending)
laws.enacted: 2026; takes effect only if the constitutional amendment passes
laws.summary: If it takes effect, a person loses the vote only while incarcerated for a felony and regains it on release. Its effective date is contingent; see Acts 2026, cc. 992 and 1081.

laws.name: Notice of how to restore rights
laws.summary: Requires the Department of Corrections to tell people with felony convictions how to apply for restoration of civil and voting rights when they finish their sentence.

laws.name: Voting Rights Act of Virginia
laws.summary: Virginia's state voting rights act, which protects voters from discrimination based on race, color or language-minority status.

laws.name: Voter suppression prohibited
laws.summary: Bars voting rules and practices that deny or abridge the right to vote on account of race, color or language-minority status.

laws.name: Vote dilution prohibited
laws.summary: Bars election methods that dilute the voting strength of protected groups.

laws.name: In-state tuition regardless of immigration status
laws.summary: Makes students who attended a Virginia high school for at least two years and graduated, and whose household filed Virginia income tax returns for two years, eligible for in-state tuition regardless of citizenship or immigration status.
check: regardless of citizenship or immigration status

laws.name: Public school regardless of immigration status
laws.summary: Guarantees a free public education and bars discrimination based on citizenship or immigration status, with a right to sue.

laws.name: No immigration questions for victims and witnesses
laws.summary: Bars officers from asking about the immigration status of crime victims and witnesses who report or help investigate a crime, with limited exceptions.

laws.name: Warning about immigration consequences
laws.summary: Requires the court to tell a defendant that a conviction can affect their immigration status.

laws.name: Immigration threats at work
laws.summary: Penalizes employers who threaten to report a worker's immigration status to coerce or retaliate.

laws.name: Banned lease terms
laws.summary: Lists lease provisions a landlord may not include, such as waiving a tenant's rights or remedies under the landlord-tenant law.

laws.name: Right of redemption
laws.summary: Lets a tenant stop an eviction for unpaid rent by paying all rent, late charges, attorney fees and court costs on or before the first court date, or within 10 days after it with a redemption tender.

laws.name: No retaliation against tenants
laws.summary: Bars landlords from raising rent, cutting services or evicting because a tenant complained about conditions, joined a tenant organization or testified.

laws.name: Breaking a lease to escape abuse
laws.summary: Lets victims of family abuse, sexual abuse, stalking or trafficking end a lease early after obtaining a protective order or other listed documentation, with written notice.

laws.name: Safe reporting of overdoses
laws.summary: A person who in good faith seeks emergency help for an overdose, stays at the scene until police arrive and identifies themself cannot be arrested or prosecuted for listed drug and alcohol offenses found because of that call. Reports of sexual violence are covered too.

laws.name: Adult marijuana possession
laws.summary: Makes possession of up to two ounces of marijuana in public lawful for adults 21 and older. Larger amounts are penalized on a sliding scale.

laws.name: Civil rights definitions
laws.summary: Defines terms for Maryland's civil rights law, including gender identity and sexual orientation.

laws.name: Equal access to public places
laws.enacted: Gender identity added by the Fairness for All Marylanders Act, 2014
laws.summary: Bars a place of public accommodation from refusing or denying service because of race, sex, age, color, creed, national origin, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or disability.

laws.name: Employment discrimination
laws.summary: Bars employers from refusing to hire, firing or discriminating in pay or conditions because of race, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, military status, disability and other traits.

laws.name: Fair housing policy
laws.summary: States Maryland's policy of fair housing for all, regardless of race, sex, familial status, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and other traits.

laws.name: Housing discrimination
laws.enacted: Source of income added by the HOME Act, 2020
laws.summary: Bars refusing to rent or sell, setting different terms, or advertising preferences on a protected basis, including source of income such as a housing voucher.

laws.name: Right to sue for job discrimination
laws.summary: Lets a person who filed a timely discrimination charge sue the employer once 180 days have passed, within 2 years of the discrimination, or 3 years for harassment.

laws.name: Marriage equality
laws.enacted: Civil Marriage Protection Act, 2012; upheld by referendum
laws.summary: A marriage between two individuals who are not otherwise prohibited from marrying is valid, regardless of sex.

laws.name: Conversion therapy ban
laws.summary: Bars licensed mental health and child care practitioners from conversion therapy on minors. A violation is unprofessional conduct.

laws.name: New birth certificate for sex designation
laws.summary: Provides a new birth certificate with a changed sex designation when a licensed health care practitioner states the person has had treatment appropriate for sex transition or has an intersex condition, or on the other routes the section lists.

laws.name: Medicaid covers gender-affirming care
laws.enacted: Trans Health Equity Act, 2023; in effect January 1, 2024
laws.summary: Requires Maryland Medicaid to cover medically necessary gender-affirming treatment, including hormones, puberty blockers, surgery, voice and hair treatment, and bars denying it because of a recipient's gender identity.
check: may not deny or limit coverage

laws.name: Legally protected health care
laws.enacted: 2023 for reproductive care; gender-affirming treatment added 2024 (SB 119)
laws.summary: Defines legally protected health care, which includes gender-affirming treatment and reproductive care. Maryland's shield protections against out-of-state subpoenas and extradition all point to this definition.

laws.name: Shield from extradition for protected care
laws.summary: Limits the Governor's power to surrender someone to another state for providing, receiving or assisting with legally protected health care in Maryland.

laws.name: Shield from out-of-state subpoenas
laws.summary: A party asking a Maryland court to issue a subpoena for another state's case must swear it is not meant to further an investigation or proceeding over legally protected health care, except narrow suits such as one brought by the patient.

laws.name: Shield for out-of-state witness summons
laws.summary: Applies the same shield to summonses compelling a Maryland witness to testify in another state about legally protected health care.

laws.name: Manslaughter and the panic-defense ban
laws.summary: Sets the penalty for manslaughter and provides that a victim's actual or perceived race, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion or disability is not adequate provocation to reduce murder to manslaughter.

laws.name: Hate crimes
laws.summary: Makes it a crime to commit an offense against a person or property because of race, color, religion, sexual orientation, sex, gender identity, disability, national origin or homelessness.

laws.name: Health plans and gender identity
laws.summary: Bars health insurance carriers from denying coverage on the basis of race, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and other listed traits.

laws.name: School bullying reporting
laws.summary: Defines bullying, harassment and intimidation in schools and requires reporting and tracking of incidents.

laws.name: Maryland Use of Force Statute
laws.summary: Police may use force only when necessary and proportional. Officers must de-escalate when safe, intervene to stop excessive force by another officer and give first aid. An intentional violation that causes serious injury or death is a crime punishable by up to 10 years.

laws.name: Police accountability boards
laws.summary: Requires every county to have a police accountability board that takes misconduct complaints from the public, appoints civilians to charging committees and trial boards, and reports each year on discipline trends.

laws.name: Body-worn cameras
laws.summary: Requires a statewide policy on body-worn cameras that covers when recording is mandatory or prohibited, notice, access, retention and release of recordings.

laws.name: Search warrants and no-knock limits
laws.summary: Governs search warrants. A no-knock warrant may be requested only with written approval from a police supervisor and the State's Attorney, on reasonable suspicion that knocking would endanger someone, and the application must lay out the evidence.
check: police supervisor and the State's Attorney

laws.name: Cannabis odor is not grounds to stop or search
laws.summary: Officers may not stop or search a person, car or boat based only on the odor of cannabis, possession of a personal-use amount, or cash near cannabis without other signs of dealing.
check: odor of burnt or unburnt cannabis

laws.name: Independent Investigations Division
laws.summary: Creates the unit in the Attorney General's office that investigates police-involved deaths and serious injuries.

laws.name: Attorney General may prosecute police
laws.summary: Lets the Attorney General prosecute offenses found in an Independent Investigations Division case.

laws.name: Police and investigation records
laws.summary: Lists the investigative and police records a custodian may withhold, including officer misconduct files, but only on the grounds the law allows. Anton's Law (2021) moved misconduct files from the always-secret personnel category into this one, so they can be requested.

laws.name: Maryland Public Information Act
laws.summary: Gives the public the right to inspect public records at any reasonable time, with denial allowed only as the law provides.

laws.name: Expungement petitions
laws.summary: Lets a person petition to expunge police and court records of charges that ended in acquittal, dismissal, probation before judgment, nolle prosequi and other listed outcomes.

laws.name: Automatic expungement
laws.summary: Automatically expunges records three years after disposition when every charge in the case ended in acquittal, dismissal, not guilty or nolle prosequi (not nolle prosequi with required treatment).

laws.name: Expunging convictions
laws.summary: Lets a person petition to expunge listed misdemeanor and felony convictions after the waiting period.

laws.name: Shielding records (Second Chance Act)
laws.summary: Lets a person petition to shield court and police records of shieldable convictions 3 years after finishing the sentence, including parole and probation, so most of the public and employers cannot see them.

laws.name: Relief for cannabis possession convictions
laws.summary: A person still incarcerated for a cannabis possession conviction can apply to be resentenced. The court must resentence them to time served and release them if they are not serving another sentence.
check: resentence the person to time served

laws.name: Writ of actual innocence
laws.summary: Lets a person convicted in circuit court petition at any time for a writ of actual innocence on newly discovered evidence. After a trial, the evidence must create a substantial or significant possibility of a different result; after a guilty plea, it must show innocence by clear and convincing evidence.

laws.name: Postconviction DNA testing
laws.summary: Lets a person convicted of serious crimes petition for DNA testing of evidence and requires the State to preserve it.

laws.name: Compensation for wrongful confinement
laws.summary: Compensates a person erroneously convicted and confined for a crime they did not commit, for each day of wrongful confinement, at a daily rate based on Maryland's median household income, once an administrative law judge finds them eligible.

laws.name: Second look for young offenders
laws.summary: Lets a person convicted as an adult for an offense committed as a minor, who has served at least 20 years, ask the court to reduce the sentence. It also covers some people who were 18 to 24 at the time.

laws.name: Medical parole
laws.summary: Allows medical parole for incarcerated people who are chronically debilitated or incapacitated, or terminally ill, when all their sentences carry the possibility of parole.

laws.name: Good Samaritan overdose law
laws.summary: A person who in good faith seeks or gives medical help for someone in a drug or alcohol emergency cannot be arrested, charged or prosecuted for listed drug offenses when the evidence came only from that call for help. Seeking help is also a mitigating factor.

laws.name: Solitary confinement reporting
laws.summary: Requires correctional units to report on restrictive housing, including people with serious mental illness, pregnant people, length of stay and deaths and self-harm.

laws.name: Pregnancy and childbirth in custody
laws.summary: Sets rules for incarcerated people who are pregnant, in labor or postpartum, including a ban on physical restraints during labor and delivery unless the responsible medical professional decides otherwise.
check: physical restraint may not be used

laws.name: Children must talk to a lawyer before interrogation
laws.summary: Police may not interrogate a child in custody until the child has consulted with an attorney and the officer has tried to notify a parent or guardian.

laws.name: Juvenile court jurisdiction
laws.summary: Sets which children juvenile court handles: delinquency cases start at age 13, or age 10 for listed serious offenses such as crimes of violence.

laws.name: Voting after a felony
laws.summary: A felony conviction bars registration only while the person is serving a court-ordered sentence of imprisonment, so voting rights return on release.
check: currently serving a court-ordered sentence of imprisonment

laws.name: No retaliatory eviction
laws.summary: Bars a landlord from suing for possession, raising rent or cutting services because a tenant complained, joined a tenants' organization or asserted their rights.

laws.name: Rent escrow for serious defects
laws.summary: Lets tenants pay rent into court when a landlord fails to repair serious and dangerous defects.

laws.name: Right to counsel in evictions
laws.summary: Gives covered tenants access to legal representation in eviction proceedings.

laws.name: Eviction for unpaid rent
laws.summary: Sets the court process a landlord must follow to evict for unpaid rent, including the tenant's right to redeem by paying.

laws.name: Ban the box
laws.summary: Employers may not ask about criminal records before the first in-person interview, with exceptions.

laws.name: Medical records are confidential
laws.summary: Requires health care providers to keep medical records confidential and to disclose them only as the law allows.

laws.name: Limits on police immigration enforcement
laws.summary: Bars police during regular duties from asking about citizenship, immigration status or place of birth during a stop, search or arrest, or detaining someone to investigate immigration status, with exceptions.

laws.name: Immigration enforcement at sensitive locations
laws.summary: Public schools, libraries and state and local agencies at sensitive locations must deny immigration enforcement agents access to nonpublic areas unless they present a valid federal court warrant or there are exigent circumstances.
check: valid warrant issued by a federal court

laws.name: Maryland Dream Act
laws.summary: Makes undocumented students who meet the attendance and other conditions eligible for in-state tuition.

laws.name: Cannabis citations, not arrests
laws.summary: Use or possession of a civil use or personal use amount of cannabis is a civil offense handled by citation, not a criminal conviction.

laws.name: Civil rights lawsuits (Section 1983)
laws.summary: Lets a person sue anyone who, acting under color of state law, deprives them of federal constitutional or statutory rights. It is the basis of most suits over police and jail abuse.

laws.name: Equal rights under the law
laws.summary: Guarantees all persons the same right to make and enforce contracts, sue and give evidence, regardless of race.

laws.name: Title VII employment discrimination
laws.enacted: 1964; Bostock v. Clayton County (2020) held that firing someone for being gay or transgender is sex discrimination
laws.summary: Bars employers from refusing to hire, firing or discriminating because of race, color, religion, sex or national origin. Coverage thresholds are in 42 U.S.C. § 2000e.

laws.name: Federal Fair Housing Act
laws.summary: Bars housing discrimination because of race, color, religion, sex, familial status or national origin, and separately because of a handicap (disability).

laws.name: ADA: public entities
laws.summary: Bars state and local governments, including courts, police, jails and prisons, from excluding or discriminating against qualified people with disabilities.

laws.name: Title VI
laws.summary: Bars discrimination on the basis of race, color or national origin in any program that receives federal money.

laws.name: Title IX
laws.summary: Bars sex discrimination in federally funded education programs.

laws.name: Federal hate crimes (Shepard-Byrd Act)
laws.summary: Makes it a federal crime to cause or attempt bodily injury because of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or disability.

laws.name: Pattern-or-practice police investigations
laws.summary: Makes it unlawful for police or juvenile justice agencies to engage in a pattern or practice of violating people's rights, and lets the U.S. Attorney General sue to stop it.

laws.name: Civil Rights of Institutionalized Persons Act
laws.summary: Lets the U.S. Attorney General sue a state or local government that subjects people in jails, prisons, juvenile facilities or other institutions to egregious or flagrant conditions.

laws.name: Prison Rape Elimination Act standards
laws.summary: Requires national standards for the detection, prevention, reduction and punishment of prison rape, which apply to prisons, jails and juvenile facilities.
check: national standards for the detection, prevention, reduction, and punishment of prison rape

laws.name: Substance use treatment records (Part 2)
laws.summary: Keeps substance use disorder treatment records confidential and limits their use against the patient in criminal cases without a court order.

laws.name: Voting Rights Act, Section 2
laws.summary: Bars any voting practice that results in denying or abridging the right to vote on account of race or color.

laws.name: ACA Section 1557
laws.summary: Bars discrimination in federally funded health programs on the grounds covered by Title VI, Title IX, the Age Discrimination Act and Section 504. Whether its sex protection covers gender identity is being litigated.
